disclaimer: All scenarios are fictional. No commands run against devices or networks.

labs.title: Recognize a safe computer workflow
labs.context: You have downloaded an unfamiliar attachment from a mock email. Decide which actions protect your device and data.
steps: A file is named invoice.pdf.exe. What do you do?
Treat it as a possible executable and verify its source
The final extension can signal an executable. A filename is not evidence of safety.
A basic calculator requests contact access. Your response?
Deny and ask why the access would be needed
Permissions should fit a documented task.
You want to protect important study notes against accidental deletion. Choose a control.
Keep a separate tested versioned backup
A separate backup can restore data after a synced deletion.

labs.title: Read a simulated Linux terminal
labs.context: You're in an isolated sample home directory, not a real machine. Interpret basic read-only commands.
steps: Two dots refer to the parent.
The -a option includes entries hidden from default listings.
You see an unfamiliar file owned by another user. What's the safe action?
Viewing another user's data requires proper authorization.

labs.title: Protect a small organization
labs.context: A fictional company is setting up employee accounts and recovery controls.
steps: No passwords and no alternate controls
Unique passwords and MFA reduce compromise risk.
An employee changes departments. What should happen?
Least privilege should reflect current duties.
A suspicious login page arrives by text. What should staff do?
Use a known official login route
The company has backups but never tests restores. What is missing?
Test restores establish whether recovery works.

labs.title: Windows security triage
labs.context: A hypothetical workstation is slow following an ordinary system update. Choose a careful investigation path.
steps: Task Manager shows high CPU. First step?
High CPU is an observation rather than a diagnosis.
A standard employee needs to browse reports. Appropriate permission?
Least privilege limits mistakes and damage.
A system update is pending on a business computer. Best plan?
Updates benefit from planning and verification.

labs.title: Troubleshoot a fictional network
labs.context: A small office can connect to Wi-Fi, but a training website fails to load. No traffic is sent in this lab.
steps: A device has no assigned IP address. What might need checking?
An IP address is reachable but a site name fails. Investigate?
Name resolution is distinct from reachability.
The guest network can reach payroll records. What is the concern?
Visitor traffic should generally be separated from sensitive systems.
A host ignores ping. Does that prove it is offline?
ICMP filtering can block echo replies on healthy hosts.

labs.title: Trace beginner programming logic
labs.context: Interpret pseudocode running entirely inside this training page.
steps: Set count=2, then count=count+1. The result?
The assignment increases the value by one.
If locked=true, which branch runs in 'if locked then deny else allow'?
The true branch performs the denial.
A loop runs once for each of 4 mock log entries. How many iterations?
A client changes a displayed role to admin. What must protect the data?

labs.title: Analyze a fictional sign-in timeline
labs.context: Mock records: 09:00 login_failed user A; 09:01 login_failed user A; 09:02 login_success user B; 09:05 software deployment began. No real accounts are involved.
steps: Which event shows confirmed successful authentication?
Only the success event confirms the recorded authentication outcome; it does not prove broader compromise.
What is justified about user A?
Failures alone do not establish intent or account compromise.
Compare timestamps with the deployment change record
Correlating approved operational change information avoids premature conclusions.
Two failures for A, one success for B, and a later deployment; root cause unknown

labs.title: Make a cloud access decision
labs.course: Applied Security Architecture and Threat Modeling
labs.context: A fictional training portal stores private grades in a cloud database. A browser requests a grade record using a student ID.
steps: Where must the access decision occur?
At the trusted API or database security layer
Client-side controls can be changed by users.
A student asks for another student's record. What should happen?
Return it because the caller logged in
Use the identifier as proof of permission
Authentication alone is not resource authorization.
What is safe to include in an access-denied log?
Time, anonymized account ID, outcome, resource category
Log enough to investigate without exposing secrets.
The service goes offline. What should the team use?
An approved recovery and communication plan

labs.title: Defensive cryptography decisions
labs.context: A fictional organization needs confidential file storage, verified software downloads, and trusted internal messaging.
steps: What primarily protects a lost laptop's stored records?
Encryption protects confidentiality of stored data.
A publisher provides a trusted file digest. What can it help check?
Whether the file is free of every bug
Compare against an authentic, trusted hash reference.
Which property does a digital signature add?
Verification of origin and integrity under trusted keys
Signatures verify authenticity and integrity but do not themselves encrypt content.
A private key is exposed publicly. What is the priority?
Revoke or rotate it and investigate exposure

labs.title: Respond to a simulated supplier fraud alert
labs.context: Mock invoice email requests a bank change for a $45,000 payment. The sender display name is familiar, but the domain has one extra character.
steps: The sender domain differs from the established one
The payment amount has a comma
How should finance verify the request?
Use an existing trusted contact method
Call the number in the suspicious message
Report through approved channels and retain relevant message details
What should a leadership memo include?
Evidence, payment delay tradeoff, verification control and decision owner
A certain accusation of the supplier
A professional memo communicates grounded tradeoffs and actions.

labs.title: Scope an ethical testing engagement
labs.context: An organization grants written permission to review a synthetic application in an isolated classroom environment only.
steps: A production server shares the same brand. Is it in scope?
No, permission must explicitly include it
Yes, any related domain is allowed
Scope is defined by the authorization.
What makes a useful test hypothesis?
A specific expected access rule and a permitted way to check it
A plan to copy private data
A claim that every endpoint is vulnerable
Hypotheses should be narrow and falsifiable.
A mock lab result suggests improper access. What next?
Record the minimum allowed evidence and report it
Data minimization and approved reporting protect others.
When can the finding be closed?
When the patch is merely proposed
Closure should be based on verification.

labs.title: Subnet and DNS Reasoning
labs.context: An isolated classroom network uses 192.168.50.0/24. One fictional learner cannot open the training portal.
steps: The 24-bit prefix identifies 192.168.50 as the first three octets.
How many conventional usable hosts are in a /24?
256 total minus network and broadcast addresses in an ordinary /24.
The learner can reach the gateway but domain lookup fails. What should be checked?
Name resolution is a separate diagnostic layer.
An HTTP 404 is returned after navigating to a URL. What has happened?
Which evidence belongs in the support ticket?
Exact observed failures, IP settings and time
A claim of an attack without indicators

labs.title: Linux Files and Permissions
labs.context: A synthetic Linux directory contains a financial report owned by a designated service account.
steps: Common Linux conventions place user data under /home.
A file has mode 640. Which group permission is represented?
What is a prerequisite for examining real private files?
Access depends on permissions and scope.
A service has high CPU during backups. What is a reasonable first move?
Resource utilization alone is not malicious evidence.
How can a team demonstrate backups are recoverable?
Trust the backup job success message only
Store all copies on one disk
Tested restoration verifies more than successful job execution.

labs.title: Identity and Session Audit
labs.context: A fictional enterprise connects the academy portal and payroll application to one identity provider.
steps: The caller proved identity to the provider
An administrator role in all systems
A former contractor retains active sessions. What is the control gap?
A reporting service needs only one bucket. Appropriate permission?
Service identities should follow least privilege.
Which factor deserves additional protection during account recovery?
Recovery paths can bypass otherwise strong authentication.
What demonstrates a successful privilege review?
Documented effective permissions and owner approval
A screenshot of the login page
The actual access granted matters more than labels.

labs.title: Web Authorization Decision Lab
labs.context: A synthetic learning API exposes /grades/learner-id and requires a signed-in student.
steps: A student changes the displayed learner ID. Who protects the resource?
Per-record checks belong on a trusted service.
A session ends in the browser. What else should happen when possible?
Effective sign-out includes revocation or expiration.
What should be logged about an access denial?
Time, account reference and denied operation
Keep useful audit metadata without leaking secrets.
After changing permissions, what constitutes validation?
Authorized tests of allowed and denied requests

labs.title: Cloud Recovery and Change Control
labs.context: A mock organization proposes an approved storage policy change before a quarter-end deadline.
steps: Tolerable data loss measured in time
RPO bounds acceptable loss of recent changes.
The date of the last patch
RTO concerns how quickly a service should be restored.
What should happen before a sensitive access policy change?
Scope, approval, testing and rollback preparation
Who configures permissions on the customer's database?
Shared responsibility includes customer identity and data controls.
Which review helps verify a fix?
Read effective policy and test access with synthetic accounts
Assume that a save button guarantees safety
Configuration and behavior must both be evaluated.

labs.title: Incident Response Timeline
labs.context: Mock data: 10:00 portal errors increase; 10:03 deployment completes; 10:08 rollback begins; 10:12 errors decrease. The root cause is unconfirmed.
steps: Errors increased before a rollback and decreased afterward
Temporal association does not establish attribution.
Correlation should be tested against technical context.
What should a status update communicate?
Which event belongs in the incident timeline?
A hypothetical event with no timestamp
Time-anchored events make the timeline auditable.
Assuming fewer errors guarantees every feature works

labs.title: Defensive Cryptography Reasoning
labs.context: A fictional software vendor distributes a signed application and publishes an authenticated file digest.
steps: What does a trusted digest comparison help assess?
Whether software is harmless in all contexts
Whether an account is an administrator
A matching digest helps detect changes relative to a trusted reference.
What does a digital signature primarily support?
Origin and integrity under trusted key assumptions
Signatures authenticate signing keys and detect alteration.
Which key should not be disclosed?
Private keys must be protected from unauthorized use.
A TLS certificate warning appears at a login page. Best action?
Stop and independently verify the site
Server authentication may be unreliable when validation fails.
A private service key is found in public source. First?
Revoke or rotate it and investigate access
Public exposure may persist after deleting a file.

labs.title: Risk Register Decision Workshop
labs.context: A fictional retailer has one internet-exposed critical service and a separate, offline training device. Both need patching.
steps: Which typically deserves first risk review?
What is a risk register entry's useful minimum?
Asset, concern, owner, treatment and review date
What counts as evidence of remediation?
An authorized retest and recorded observation
A test target is outside written scope. Action?
Do not test without updated permission
Impact, priorities, options, uncertainty and recommended actions
Decisions require summarized tradeoffs and factual boundaries.

labs.title: Portable access and RFID hardware
labs.context: Synthetic training covering Flipper Zero, Proxmark3 and O.MG Cable. No physical device interaction or real traffic.
steps: A fictional RFID tag displays a public identifier. Does that prove authorization?
Only if a tool is expensive
Tag identity alone is not authentication.
A mock badge test is documented. What is its evidence boundary?
Simulation does not establish production findings.
A cable looks ordinary but is unapproved. Appropriate response?
Plug it into a privileged workstation
Physical appearance does not establish trust.
Accurate limitations, safe setup and reporting
A device does not confer authorization.

labs.title: Wireless security hardware
labs.context: Synthetic training covering WiFi Pineapple, HackRF One and Alfa Wi-Fi Adapter. No physical device interaction or real traffic.
steps: A mock client connects to a similarly named access point. Priority?
Assume every Wi-Fi network is malicious
What should an introductory radio lab use?
Safe training preserves spectrum rules and privacy.
What is packet analysis primarily based on?
Observed metadata and authorized traffic evidence
Packet records require careful contextual interpretation.
What is required for any real active wireless assessment?

labs.title: USB and network appliances
labs.context: Synthetic training covering USB Rubber Ducky, Bash Bunny and Shark Jack. No physical device interaction or real traffic.
steps: An unexpected USB keyboard event appears. Next action?
What is the safest training replacement for an automated USB demonstration?
Borrowing someone else's laptop without asking
Simulation teaches concepts without unintended actions.
Where should a wired testing appliance be attached?
Only an explicitly approved lab interface
Physical connection does not grant consent.
Explain event evidence and unresolved uncertainty
Claim all network traffic is compromised
Evidence and reporting support defensible conclusions.

labs.title: Microcontrollers and electronic instruments
labs.context: Synthetic training covering Raspberry Pi, ESP32 Marauder and Logic Analyzer. No physical device interaction or real traffic.
steps: What makes a beginner Raspberry Pi network lab appropriate?
Lab isolation and secure defaults reduce risk.
A microcontroller displays synthetic Bluetooth metadata. What may be concluded?
Only the metadata shown in the exercise
Synthetic observations do not confer authorization.
What does a logic analyzer measure?
What is the correct graduation evidence for physical hardware operation?
Physical proficiency requires actual supervised demonstration.
